ASPIRATION_PNEUMONIA.title: Aspiration pneumonia (lung infection from breathing in food or fluid)

items: Aspiration pneumonia is an infection of the lung that follows breathing food, drink, saliva or vomit into the lungs.
It is more likely if you have reduced consciousness or trouble swallowing (dysphagia).
Fever, cough, and sometimes chest crackles on examination.
Foul-smelling sputum (mucus you cough up) can occur.
Chest X-ray. The shadow is usually in the lower lobes or back parts of the lungs.
Blood tests such as a blood count and CRP (a marker of inflammation).
A swallowing assessment if the problem keeps coming back.
Your doctor will decide on treatment based on your condition.
A swallowing assessment can guide safer feeding.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Sit upright when eating and drinking, if your doctor advises it.
Tell your doctor or nurse about any coughing or choking with meals.
Keep your review appointments and tell your doctor if breathing or swallowing gets worse.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Fever with rising breathlessness or confusion
Coughing up large amounts of foul sputum, or a fall in alertness
